title: AdFection: Targeted ads turned into a pipeline for zero-click mercenary spyware
titleZh: AdFection：定向广告变成了零点击雇佣间谍软件的管道
author: jcomp
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Devices at international news network Al Jazeera were infected with mercenary spyware from Candiru (rebranded as “Integrity Labs”) via targeted online advertisements. We provide the first public technical confirmation of a zero-click mercenary spyware attack delivered via targeted advertising, which we call AdFection.

The malicious advertisements were purchased by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that presents itself as a legitimate advertising company, but which we found operates as a facilitator for multiple mercenary spyware partners.

Discover-Tech operates a platform called Controlium that enables its mercenary partners to de-anonymize, fingerprint, and automatically infect devices the moment an advertisement is rendered — a form of zero-click attack.

Analysis of four billion Discover-Tech bidding records shows that during a four-month period, the company’s ads were shown on almost 200,000 unique websites and Android/iOS apps in dozens of countries.
summaryZh: Devices at international news network Al Jazeera were infected with mercenary spyware from Candiru (rebranded as “Integrity Labs”) via targeted online advertisements. We provide the first public technical confirmation of a zero-click mercenary spyware attack delivered via targeted advertising, which we call AdFection.

comments.author: ferguess_k
comments.textRawHtml:
My question is, why is Israel so good at this? It seems to be at least the 4th cyber power of the world, after the US, Russia and China, if not actually on par or better.

I guess it is because it has been under the threat of larger enemies from its birth, so it must leverage whatever it has to survive. And once you grow an organization and let it loose, you don't have much control over it anymore, and it grows in the wild like a flower.
comments.textZhHtml:
我的问题是，为什么以色列在这方面如此擅长？它似乎至少是继美国、俄罗斯和中国之后的世界第四网络强国，即使实际上不是同等或更好。

我想这是因为它从诞生之日起就受到更大敌人的威胁，所以它必须利用一切手段来生存。一旦你发展了一个组织并让它自由发展，你就不再对它有太多的控制权，它就会像花朵一样在野外生长。

children.author: deepsun
children.textRawHtml:
Don't forget the compounding effect. Say, one country (or city or community) decides to invest their efforts into area X (e.g. clock making in Switzerland). They do it and become better and better. As long as they keep doing that they can become #1 in the world. Regardless of any reasons "why them".

There's no reason Netherlands are better at chip lithography except that they're doing it (Dutch agriculture success can be attributed to good soils/climate/geolocation, but not chips). There's no reason Hollywood is better at filmmaking. Kinda chaos theory -- small changes to initial state leads to huge changes in the later outcomes.
children.textZhHtml:
不要忘记复合效应。比如说，一个国家（或城市或社区）决定将其精力投入到 X 领域（例如瑞士的钟表制造）。他们这样做并且变得越来越好。只要他们继续这样做，他们就能成为世界第一。不管“为什么”有任何原因。

荷兰没有理由在芯片光刻方面做得更好，除非他们正在这样做（荷兰农业的成功可以归因于良好的土壤/气候/地理位置，但不是芯片）。好莱坞没有理由更擅长电影制作。有点混沌理论——初始状态的微小变化会导致后来结果的巨大变化。

children.author: BunsanSpace
children.textRawHtml:
I would like to give a real world example of this too.

If you want to do something artistic or start a business based around Art, Montreal is perfect for it, for the very same reason above.

Initially the govt invested in the arts to preserve French culture, which resulted in a lot of art infrastructure being made, cheap ateliers, fabric suppliers, paint suppliers, &c. Which attracted a lot of artists, which then increases the demand for the art infrastructure, which makes the city easy to make art in.

It makes it stupid easy to make stuff and find the skilled artisans you need to make it. Much easier than any other Canadian city I've lived in.
children.textZhHtml:
我也想举一个现实世界的例子。

如果你想做一些艺术或以艺术为基础的生意，蒙特利尔是完美的选择，原因与上述相同。

最初政府投资艺术是为了保护法国文化，这导致了许多艺术基础设施的建立，廉价的工作室、织物供应商、油漆供应商等。这吸引了很多艺术家，从而增加了对艺术基础设施的需求，这使得这座城市很容易制作艺术品。

这使得制作东西并找到制作所需的熟练工匠变得非常容易。比我住过的任何其他加拿大城市都要容易得多。

children.author: gumby
children.textRawHtml:
The Hollywood case has a quirk that is relevent to the extensional content of HN:

West coast filmmakng started in the Bay Area (at the time the largest conurbation in the west) but moved south because of the year 'round weather.

But why the west? Because Edison controlled the filmmaking patents and demanded not just royalties but script oversight as well. By moving west, they could ignore the patents because they were simply too hard to enforce from such a long distance.

So ironically, given how things worked out, IP piracy is at the root of Hollywood.
children.textZhHtml:
好莱坞案例有一个与 HN 的外延内容相关的怪癖：

西海岸电影制作始于湾区（当时是西部最大的城市），但由于全年天气而向南移动。

但是为什么是西部呢？ 因为爱迪生控制着电影制作专利，不仅要求版税，还要求剧本监督。 通过向西转移，他们可以忽略这些专利，因为从这么远的距离执行这些专利太难了。

具有讽刺意味的是，考虑到事情的发展，知识产权盗版是好莱坞的根源。

children.author: deepsun
children.textRawHtml: Yep, but Edison is long gone, while Hollywood kept compounding over time. There's zero other reasons Hollywood is _currently_ better than any other place for filmmaking.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，但爱迪生早已去世，而好莱坞却随着时间的推移而不断复合。好莱坞_目前_比任何其他电影制作地方都要好，没有其他原因。

children.author: mitxela
children.textRawHtml:
Traditional Judaism has this really weird (to me, a goy) emphasis on finding loopholes in rules. I always remember these ropes they place around New York City and other places so they can stay "indoors" on, I think it was, the Shabbat, by walking underneath the rope, which is a type of ceiling.

As I understand it, they know God's not stupid and sees right through this sort of thing, but they believe God put rules like "stay indoors on the Shabbat" in place so that He could entertain Himself by watching the creative loopholes humans come up with. Other Shabbat loopholes include putting things on timers the day before, paying a non-Jew to do things that Jews are forbidden to do, or legally transferring ownership of the cupboard full of bread to a non-Jew for the one day a year when Jews aren't allowed to own bread.

And as I understand it, they do this with all things, from a young age. Cultivating this mindset definitely has something to do with their cybersecurity prowess.
children.textZhHtml:
传统犹太教非常奇怪（对我来说，一个非犹太人）强调寻找规则中的漏洞。我一直记得他们在纽约市和其他地方放置的这些绳子，这样他们就可以在安息日呆在“室内”，我认为那是安息日，在绳子下面行走，这是一种天花板。

据我了解，他们知道上帝并不愚蠢，并且能看穿这类事情，但他们相信上帝制定了诸如“安息日呆在室内”之类的规则，以便他可以通过观察人类提出的创造性漏洞来娱乐自己。安息日的其他漏洞包括在前一天把东西放在计时器上，付钱给非犹太人去做犹太人被禁止做的事情，或者在一年中不允许犹太人拥有面包的那一天合法地将装满面包的橱柜的所有权转让给非犹太人。

据我所知，他们从很小的时候就对所有东西都这样做。培养这种心态肯定与他们的网络安全能力有关。

children.author: yonatan8070
children.textRawHtml:
> Traditional Judaism has this really weird (to me, a goy) emphasis on finding loopholes in rules.

As an atheist Jew, it's weird to me as well...

> stay "indoors" on, I think it was, the Shabbat

Can't say I'm familiar with that one. What I'm generally familiar with is that you're not allowed to "work" on Shabbat, and the definition of work is extremely broad. For example, lighting a fire is considered work, turning a light switch on creates a tiny spark between the contacts, that counts as fire, so it's work.

This extends to pretty much every electrical device, so for those who observe Shabbat, using a computer or phone, turning the AC on or off, is all disallowed.

As a result there are many workarounds as you've described, timers, non-Jews (though you can't ask directly! You can say "it's hot in here", but not "Please turn the AC on"), fridges without a light bulb inside, and more.

> they do this with all things, from a young age.

Religious families do, to varying degrees. But I've met plenty of extremely talented programmers and hackers who do not follow any of the Jewish law.

Edit: Just noticed your username, I also want to say I really like your projects on YouTube!

作为一个无神论者犹太人，这对我来说也很奇怪......

> 留在“室内”，我认为那是安息日

不能说我熟悉那个。我通常熟悉的是，安息日不允许“工作”，而且工作的定义非常广泛。例如，生火被认为是工作，打开电灯开关会在触点之间产生微小的火花，这被视为火，所以它是工作。

这几乎延伸到所有电气设备，因此对于那些遵守安息日的人来说，使用电脑或手机打开或关闭空调都是不允许的。

因此，正如您所描述的，有很多解决方法，计时器，非犹太人（尽管您不能直接询问！您可以说“这里很热”，但不能说“请打开空调”），里面没有灯泡的冰箱等等。

>他们从很小的时候就对所有东西都这样做。

宗教家庭在不同程度上这样做。但我遇到了很多非常有才华的程序员和黑客，他们不遵守任何犹太法律。
